paragraphs.zh: Tabelle 1b: Vorprodukte der Verbindungen in Tabelle 1a
paragraphs.en: Table 1b: Precursors of the compounds in Table 1a
paragraphs.notes: The caption is printed with 'Tabelle 1b:' in bold and the rest in the regular face. It is the only German prose sentence on the page. It fixes the whole of Tabelle 1b as precursor (Vorprodukt) compounds for the corresponding numbered compounds of Tabelle 1a, so the numbering 3b, 4b, 5b, 9b pairs with 3, 4, 5, 9 of Tabelle 1a; the page itself does not state that pairing in words, so it is not asserted here beyond what the caption says.

The zh and en fields are identical because the cells are chemical symbols and NMR data, not German prose. The only German words in the table are the two header cells 'Nr.' and 'Physikalische Daten' ('No.' and 'Physical data'), left as printed in both fields so the transcription stays a faithful copy of the row grid. Typography as printed: the header cells R1 and R7 carry superscript 1 and 7; the digits in OCH2CF3, O(CH2)2O(CH2)2OEt, Me2SO, CDCl3 and every nH proton count are printed as subscripts and are rendered inline here; the '1' of '1H NMR' is a superscript; the 'd6' of Me2SO-d6 is printed in italic with a subscript 6. The chemical shift symbol printed at the head of each data cell is a lower case Greek delta; it is written 'd' here to keep the transcription ASCII. Spacing is as printed, including the wide gap after the colon-delta in rows 4b, 5b and 9b and the double spaces inside the 4b and 9b data. Row 5b has no text in its R1 cell: the substituent is drawn there and is recorded in drawings. The Nr. column runs 3b, 4b, 5b, 9b with no 6b, 7b or 8b; the gap is as printed and nothing is missing from the scan. Every row has H in the R7 column.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st, centred between the Tabelle 1b caption and the table header row; the generic scaffold the table enumerates
structures.core: benzene ring, drawn with three inner double bonds
substituents: COOH at C1, drawn as HO-C(=O)- with the OH written to the left and the doubly bonded O above
CH2-R1 at C3, drawn as a bond from the ring to a CH2 vertex and a further bond from that vertex up to the label R with superscript 1
SO2CH3 at C4, drawn as a bond from the ring to S, with two doubly bonded O below the S and CH3 to its right
H at C5 (drawn as a plain ring vertex, no label)
H at C6 (drawn as a plain ring vertex, no label)

drawings.notes: The locants above are a reading convention for this record: C1 is the carboxyl-bearing carbon and the numbering runs towards the chlorine, which is on the adjacent carbon as drawn. Positions are read off the drawing only. The ring substitution pattern is unambiguous in the scan: COOH, Cl, CH2R1 and SO2CH3 sit on four consecutive ring carbons, and the two remaining vertices, both on the lower left edge, are unlabelled. name and smiles are null because R1 is an undefined variable on this page; writing either would mean choosing a value R1 does not have here. presented_as is intermediate_structure because Tabelle 1b is captioned as the Vorprodukte (precursors) of the Tabelle 1a compounds, so this scaffold is a synthetic intermediate of the invention's own compounds and is not prior art. R7 appears as a table column but is not drawn on this scaffold; see discrepancies.

structures.position_in_drawing: inside the R1 cell of the table, row Nr. 5b
structures.core: tetrahydro-2H-pyran (oxane), a saturated six-membered ring with one ring oxygen, drawn with the O at the top right of the ring
substituents: at the ring carbon adjacent to the ring oxygen (C2 of the oxane): a CH2 vertex, and from that CH2 a bond to an O which is drawn with a free bond stub to its left
the free bond on that terminal O is the attachment point of the whole fragment to the scaffold above the table, at the benzylic CH2 that carries R1
structures.name: (tetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-yl)methoxy

drawings.notes: This is the R1 substituent for table row Nr. 5b, drawn instead of written because it is a ring. Every atom and bond in the cell is legible: the ring O and the exocyclic O are both labelled, the ring is saturated with no double bonds drawn, and the CH2 sits between the exocyclic O and the ring carbon next to the ring O, so the fragment is (tetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-yl)methoxy. smiles is left null because this is a table row substituent, which the run's instructions say not to render as SMILES, and because the fragment has an open valence rather than being a complete molecule. The 5b proton count in the same row, 1.55 (m,6H) plus 3.65 (m,2H) plus 4.0 (m,2H) plus 4.35 (m,1H), is consistent with the drawn ring, but the structure recorded here is read from the drawing alone.

discrepancies.what: The table has an R7 column, filled with H in all four rows, but no R7 label appears anywhere on the drawn scaffold above it.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The benzene ring carries COOH, Cl, CH2R1 and SO2CH3 on four consecutive carbons and two unlabelled plain ring vertices; there is no R7 label and no bond drawn to any R7.
discrepancies.text_says: The table header row reads Nr. | R1 | R7 | Physikalische Daten, and rows 3b, 4b, 5b and 9b each carry H in the R7 column.

illegible: A small ink blob about 1.5 characters wide sits in the white space to the right of the drawn scaffold, roughly level with the Cl label and about two thirds of the way across the page. It has the rough shape of a numeral 3 with a stroke through it but is too degraded to read and is not aligned with any text line or drawing; it is most likely a scan or photocopy artifact rather than a printed character.
